records.source: וַֽיְהִי֙ בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם וַיִּקְבְּצ֨וּ פְלִשְׁתִּ֤ים אֶת־מַֽחֲנֵיהֶם֙ לַצָּבָ֔א לְהִלָּחֵ֖ם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אָכִישׁ֙ אֶל־דָּוִ֔ד יָדֹ֣עַ תֵּדַ֗ע כִּ֤י אִתִּי֙ תֵּצֵ֣א בַֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה אַתָּ֖ה וַאֲנָשֶֽׁיךָ׃
records.gloss: And it was in the days those, and gathered [the] Philistines their camps for the army to fight against Israel; and said Achish to David, Surely you will know that with me you will go out in the camp, you and your men.
pieces: In those days the Philistines brought their forces together for war, to fight against Israel. Achish told David, "Understand this clearly: you and your men are going out to battle with me, in my army."

L.1: And it came about in those days that the Philistines gathered their camps for war, to fight against Israel. And Achish said to David, "You surely know that you will go out with me in the camp, you and your men."

R.1: At that time the Philistines brought all their troops together to go to war against Israel. Achish said to David, "You know, of course, that you and your men will march out with me and my army."

decisions.choice: their camps; the camp: the army, gathered in its camps
decisions.reason: The word means a camp, and from that the army that lives in it. The plural here pictures the troops of the several Philistine cities coming together (6:17-18; 29:2). In Achish's words, "the camp" is his own army.

decisions.choice: you surely know: Achish takes David's loyalty for granted
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for emphasis: "knowing, you will know". Achish is not asking David; he is telling him what he expects of him. He believes David has made himself hated by Israel and will serve him for good (27:12).

decisions.choice: Achish and David: David is living as a vassal of the Philistine king of Gath
decisions.reason: David had fled from Saul to Achish king of Gath and been given the town of Ziklag (27:1-7). A vassal was expected to bring his men when his lord went to war, so David is caught between his host and his own people. The story of how he escapes the battle is told in 29:1-11.

decisions.choice: forces; army (Balanced); troops; army (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "forces", "troops" and "army" for the people in the camps, since "camps" alone would sound like the tents rather than the soldiers. Literal keeps "camps" and "camp".

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר דָּוִד֙ אֶל־אָכִ֔ישׁ לָכֵן֙ אַתָּ֣ה תֵדַ֔ע אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־יַעֲשֶׂ֖ה עַבְדֶּ֑ךָ וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אָכִישׁ֙ אֶל־דָּוִ֔ד לָכֵ֗ן שֹׁמֵ֧ר לְרֹאשִׁ֛י אֲשִֽׂימְךָ֖ כָּל־הַיָּמִֽים׃פ
records.gloss: And said David to Achish, Therefore you will know what will do your servant. And said Achish to David, Therefore [a] keeper of my head I will make you all the days.
pieces: David answered Achish, "Very well, you will see for yourself what your servant will do." Achish said to David, "Very well, I will make you my bodyguard for life."

L.2: And David said to Achish, "Therefore you will know what your servant will do." And Achish said to David, "Therefore I will make you keeper of my head all the days."

R.2: David answered, "Good. Then you will see for yourself what I will do." Achish said, "Good. I will make you my own bodyguard for as long as you live."

decisions.choice: you will know what your servant will do: an answer that can be heard two ways
decisions.reason: Achish hears a promise to fight well for him. But David does not say whose side he will fight on, and the reader knows he has been deceiving Achish about his raids (27:8-12). The words are left open, as David leaves them; the question is settled only when the Philistine commanders send him away (29:4-11).

decisions.choice: therefore: very well, in that case
decisions.reason: The word usually means "therefore". Here each man uses it to take up what the other has said: "if that is so, then ...". Achish's reply rewards David in advance for what he expects David to do.

decisions.choice: keeper of my head: my bodyguard
decisions.reason: The one who guards the king's head is the guard closest to his person. Achish gives David the highest mark of trust. "All the days" means for the rest of David's life.

decisions.choice: your servant: a polite way of saying "I"
decisions.reason: Speaking of oneself as "your servant" was the humble form of address to a king or lord (17:32, 34; 20:7).

decisions.choice: I
decisions.reason: Readable puts the polite "your servant" into the plain "I". Literal and Balanced keep the humble form of address.

records.source: וּשְׁמוּאֵ֣ל מֵ֔ת וַיִּסְפְּדוּ־לוֹ֙ כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיִּקְבְּרֻ֥הוּ בָרָמָ֖ה וּבְעִיר֑וֹ וְשָׁא֗וּל הֵסִ֛יר הָאֹב֥וֹת וְאֶת־הַיִּדְּעֹנִ֖ים מֵהָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And Samuel had died, and mourned for him all Israel, and they buried him in Ramah, even in his city; and Saul had removed the mediums and the spiritists from the land.
pieces: Now Samuel was dead. All Israel had mourned for him, and they had buried him in Ramah, his own town. And Saul had removed the mediums and the spiritists from the land.

L.3: Now Samuel had died, and all Israel had mourned for him and buried him in Ramah, in his own city. And Saul had removed the mediums and the spiritists from the land.

R.3: Samuel had died some time before. All the people of Israel had mourned for him, and they had buried him in Ramah, his hometown. Saul had also forced out of the land the people who say they can talk with the dead or with spirits.

decisions.choice: Samuel had died ... Saul had removed: background, told before the story begins
decisions.reason: Both clauses put the subject first and use a verb form that looks back. They are not new events but two facts the reader needs for what follows: Samuel, whom Saul will ask for, is dead, and the people Saul will go to have been banned by Saul himself.

decisions.choice: Samuel's death and burial repeat 25:1
decisions.reason: Samuel's death, Israel's mourning and his burial at Ramah were told in 25:1 in almost the same words. They are repeated here to set the scene.

decisions.choice: the mediums and the spiritists: people who claimed to call up the dead and learn from them
decisions.reason: These are the two words forbidden together in Leviticus 19:31; 20:6, 27 and Deuteronomy 18:11. The first may name the spirit of a dead person, or the pit through which it was called up, or the one who called it; in this chapter it is used both for the people (verses 3, 9) and for the spirit (verses 7, 8). The second comes from the verb "know" and names one who claims secret knowledge from the spirits.

decisions.choice: Saul had removed them: he had kept the law against them
decisions.reason: The law forbade consulting such people and made them liable to death (Leviticus 20:27; Deuteronomy 18:10-12). Saul had once enforced it; the woman says in verse 9 that he "cut them off". The story turns on his doing what he himself had banned.

decisions.choice: the people who say they can talk with the dead or with spirits
decisions.reason: Readable describes what mediums and spiritists claimed to do, as at Leviticus 19:31. It adds "some time before" to show that Samuel's death is not part of the new events.

records.heading: Saul and the medium at Endor

records.source: וַיִּקָּבְצ֣וּ פְלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ וַיַּחֲנ֣וּ בְשׁוּנֵ֑ם וַיִּקְבֹּ֤ץ שָׁאוּל֙ אֶת־כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בַּגִּלְבֹּֽעַ׃
records.gloss: And gathered [the] Philistines and came and encamped at Shunem; and gathered Saul all Israel, and they encamped at Gilboa.
pieces: The Philistines assembled and came and camped at Shunem, and Saul gathered all Israel, and they camped at Gilboa.

L.4: And the Philistines gathered and came and camped at Shunem; and Saul gathered all Israel, and they camped at Gilboa.

R.4: The Philistines came together and set up camp at the town of Shunem. Saul called together all the fighting men of Israel, and they set up camp on Mount Gilboa.

decisions.choice: Shunem and Gilboa: two heights facing each other across the valley of Jezreel
decisions.reason: Shunem was a town in Issachar (Joshua 19:18) on the slope of the hill of Moreh, on the north side of the valley. Gilboa is the ridge on the south side. The Philistines had marched far north of their own land, into the broad valley where their chariots could move (31:1-3; 2 Samuel 1:6).

decisions.choice: all Israel: the whole army of Israel
decisions.reason: Saul gathers the fighting men from the tribes, not every person in Israel.

decisions.choice: the order of the story
decisions.reason: Chapter 29 begins with the Philistines gathering at Aphek, before they went up to Jezreel (29:1, 11). The writer tells Saul's night at Endor first and then goes back to tell what happened to David at the same time. The battle itself is told in chapter 31.

decisions.choice: the town of Shunem; Mount Gilboa; the fighting men of Israel
decisions.reason: Readable says what kind of place each name is, and that "all Israel" here means Israel's soldiers.

records.source: וַיַּ֥רְא שָׁא֖וּל אֶת־מַחֲנֵ֣ה פְלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וַיִּרָ֕א וַיֶּחֱרַ֥ד לִבּ֖וֹ מְאֹֽד׃
records.gloss: And saw Saul the camp of [the] Philistines, and he was afraid, and trembled his heart greatly.
pieces: When Saul saw the Philistine army, he was afraid, and his heart shook violently.

L.5: And Saul saw the camp of the Philistines, and he was afraid, and his heart trembled greatly.

R.5: When Saul saw the Philistine army, he became afraid. He was shaking with fear inside.

decisions.choice: his heart trembled greatly: he was filled with terror
decisions.reason: The heart is the inner person. Its trembling is deep fear, as when Eli's heart trembled for the ark (4:13). Saul and the army had been afraid before Goliath too (17:11), but then God had given David the victory.

decisions.choice: the camp of the Philistines: the Philistine army in its camp
decisions.reason: As in verse 1, the camp means the army encamped. From Gilboa Saul could look across the valley to Shunem.

decisions.choice: his heart shook violently (Balanced); he was shaking with fear inside (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of the heart; Readable says plainly that the trembling was inward fear.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁאַ֤ל שָׁאוּל֙ בַּֽיהוָ֔ה וְלֹ֥א עָנָ֖הוּ יְהוָ֑ה גַּ֧ם בַּחֲלֹמ֛וֹת גַּ֥ם בָּאוּרִ֖ים גַּ֥ם בַּנְּבִיאִֽם׃
records.gloss: And inquired Saul of Yahweh, and not answered him Yahweh, neither by dreams nor by Urim nor by prophets.
pieces: Saul inquired of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, but {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} did not answer him, whether by dreams or by the Urim or by prophets.

L.6: And Saul inquired of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, but {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} did not answer him, neither by dreams nor by Urim nor by prophets.

R.6: Saul asked {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} what he should do. But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} did not answer him. He gave Saul no answer in dreams, or through the Urim the priest used, or through prophets.

decisions.choice: the LORD did not answer him: the silence of God toward Saul
decisions.reason: Dreams, the priest's lots and prophets were the ways God was known to answer his people (Numbers 12:6; 27:21; Deuteronomy 18:15). None of them answers Saul. God had already been silent once when Saul asked (14:37), and the Spirit of Yahweh had left him (16:14). 1 Chronicles 10:13-14 gives the outcome: Saul died because he consulted a medium and did not seek Yahweh.

decisions.choice: Urim: the sacred lots by which the priest asked God for a decision
decisions.reason: The Urim were kept by the high priest with the ephod (Exodus 28:30; Numbers 27:21; 14:41 in this book). The priest Abiathar had fled to David with the ephod after Saul killed the priests of Nob (22:20; 23:6, 9). The text does not say how Saul inquired by Urim; another priest may have served him.

decisions.choice: inquired: asked God for guidance
decisions.reason: The verb "ask" sounds like Saul's own name, which means "asked for". The man whom the people asked for as king (8:10; 12:13) now asks and is not answered.

decisions.choice: the Urim the priest used; He gave Saul no answer
decisions.reason: Readable adds who used the Urim, and repeats the verb so that each of the three ways stands clearly.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר שָׁא֜וּל לַעֲבָדָ֗יו בַּקְּשׁוּ־לִי֙ אֵ֣שֶׁת בַּעֲלַת־א֔וֹב וְאֵלְכָ֥ה אֵלֶ֖יהָ וְאֶדְרְשָׁה־בָּ֑הּ וַיֹּאמְר֤וּ עֲבָדָיו֙ אֵלָ֔יו הִנֵּ֛ה אֵ֥שֶׁת בַּֽעֲלַת־א֖וֹב בְּעֵ֥ין דּֽוֹר׃
records.gloss: And said Saul to his servants, Seek for me a woman, a mistress of a spirit, and I will go to her and inquire of her. And said his servants to him, Behold, a woman, a mistress of a spirit, at Endor.
pieces: Saul told his servants, "Look for a woman who is a medium, so that I may go and inquire through her." His servants answered him, "There is a woman at Endor who is a medium."

L.7: And Saul said to his servants, "Seek out for me a woman who is mistress of a spirit, so that I may go to her and inquire of her." And his servants said to him, "Look, [there is] a woman who is mistress of a spirit at Endor."

R.7: Saul told his servants, "Find a woman for me who can call up the spirits of the dead. I will go to her and ask her what to do." His servants answered, "There is a woman like that at Endor."

decisions.choice: a woman who is mistress of a spirit: a woman who claims to call up and control a spirit of the dead
alternatives: a woman who owns a spirit pit
decisions.reason: Literally "a woman, a mistress of an 'ov". Here 'ov names the spirit, or the means of calling it, and the woman is its "owner" or "mistress", the one who has power over it. She is one of the mediums Saul himself had banned (verse 3).

decisions.choice: inquire of her: seek from the dead what only God can tell
decisions.reason: The verb is the usual one for seeking God's word (9:9). The law forbids seeking it from the dead (Deuteronomy 18:11), and Isaiah 8:19 asks why a people should seek the dead on behalf of the living instead of their God.

decisions.choice: Endor: a town on the north side of the hill of Moreh
decisions.reason: Endor lay in the land of Manasseh (Joshua 17:11), a few miles north of Shunem. To reach it from Gilboa, Saul had to go around the Philistine camp, which is one reason he went by night and in disguise (verse 8).

decisions.choice: his servants: Saul's attendants
decisions.reason: These are the men who served the king closely, here trusted to find the woman and keep the visit secret (verses 8, 23, 25).

decisions.choice: a woman who is a medium (Balanced); a woman who can call up the spirits of the dead (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the word "medium" used for this practice in Leviticus 19:31 and Deuteronomy 18:11; Readable says what she claimed to do. Literal keeps the Hebrew picture, "mistress of a spirit".

records.source: וַיִּתְחַפֵּ֣שׂ שָׁא֗וּל וַיִּלְבַּשׁ֙ בְּגָדִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֔ים וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ ה֗וּא וּשְׁנֵ֤י אֲנָשִׁים֙ עִמּ֔וֹ וַיָּבֹ֥אוּ אֶל־הָאִשָּׁ֖ה לָ֑יְלָה וַיֹּ֗אמֶר קָֽסֳמִי־נָ֥אלִי֙ בָּא֔וֹב וְהַ֣עֲלִי לִ֔י אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־אֹמַ֖ר אֵלָֽיִךְ׃
records.gloss: And disguised himself Saul and put on garments other, and went he and two men with him, and they came to the woman by night; and he said, Divine please for me by the spirit, and bring up for me whom I say to you.
pieces: So Saul disguised himself by putting on other clothes, and he set out with two men. They came to the woman at night, and he said, "Please consult the spirit for me, and bring up for me the one I name to you."

L.8: And Saul disguised himself and put on other clothes, and he went, and two men with him, and they came to the woman by night. And he said, "Please divine for me by the spirit, and bring up for me the one whom I name to you."

R.8: So Saul put on different clothes so that no one would know who he was. He went with two men, and they came to the woman during the night. Saul said to her, "Please use your spirit to find out the future for me. Bring up from the dead the person I name to you."

decisions.choice: divine for me by the spirit: seek hidden knowledge through the spirit she controls
decisions.reason: The verb is the general word for divination, forbidden to Israel in Deuteronomy 18:10. Samuel had told Saul that rebellion is like the sin of divination, using the noun of the same root (15:23). Saul now asks for the very thing.

decisions.choice: bring up: call up from below
decisions.reason: The dead were thought of as below, in the earth or in Sheol (2:6), so calling one of them was "bringing up" (verses 11, 13-15; Isaiah 29:4).

decisions.choice: he disguised himself ... by night: so as not to be known
decisions.reason: Saul hides who he is from the woman, who would fear him (verse 9), and goes at night, perhaps also to pass the Philistine camp unseen. The tall king (9:2) cannot simply be a stranger.

decisions.choice: so that no one would know who he was; use your spirit to find out the future; from the dead
decisions.reason: Readable says why Saul changed his clothes, what divining meant, and where he wanted someone brought up from.

records.source: וַתֹּ֨אמֶר הָֽאִשָּׁ֜ה אֵלָ֗יו הִנֵּ֨ה אַתָּ֤ה יָדַ֨עְתָּ֙ אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֣ה שָׁא֔וּל אֲשֶׁ֥ר הִכְרִ֛ית אֶת־הָאֹב֥וֹת וְאֶת־הַיִּדְּעֹנִ֖י מִן־הָאָ֑רֶץ וְלָמָ֥ה אַתָּ֛ה מִתְנַקֵּ֥שׁ בְּנַפְשִׁ֖י לַהֲמִיתֵֽנִי׃
records.gloss: And said the woman to him, Behold, you know what has done Saul, how he has cut off the mediums and the spiritist from the land; and why [are] you laying a snare for my life to cause me to die?
pieces: But the woman said to him, "Surely you know what Saul has done, how he has cut off the mediums and the spiritists from the land. Why then are you setting a trap for my life, to get me killed?"

L.9: And the woman said to him, "Look, you know what Saul has done, how he has cut off the mediums and the spiritists from the land. Then why are you laying a snare for my life, to bring about my death?"

R.9: But the woman said, "You know what Saul has done. He has gotten rid of everyone in the land who talks with the dead or with spirits. So why are you trying to trap me? Do you want me to be put to death?"

decisions.choice: cut off: removed, perhaps by putting them to death
decisions.reason: Verse 3 says Saul "removed" them. "Cut off" can mean to drive out or to destroy, and the law set death as the penalty (Leviticus 20:27). The text does not say which Saul did; the woman fears for her life either way.

decisions.choice: laying a snare for my life: trying to trap me into a crime that carries death
decisions.reason: She suspects that the stranger is an informer or a trap set by the king.

decisions.choice: you know what Saul has done: she speaks of Saul to Saul
decisions.reason: The woman does not know she is talking to the king. The reader does, and hears the irony.

decisions.choice: the spiritists: one word used for the whole group
decisions.reason: The second word is singular here, unlike verse 3, but it names the whole class of such people.

decisions.choice: Do you want me to be put to death?
decisions.reason: Readable splits the question in two, and describes the mediums and spiritists as in verse 3.

records.source: וַיִּשָּׁ֤בַֽע לָהּ֙ שָׁא֔וּל בַּֽיהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר חַי־יְהוָ֕ה אִֽם־יִקְּרֵ֥ךְ עָוֺ֖ן בַּדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: And swore to her Saul by Yahweh, saying, [As] lives Yahweh, if will befall you punishment in the matter this.
pieces: Saul gave her his oath by {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: "As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives, no punishment will come on you for this."

L.10: And Saul swore to her by {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, saying, "[As] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives, no punishment shall befall you in this matter."

R.10: Saul made a promise to her in the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He said, "As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives, you will not be punished for doing this."

decisions.choice: as the LORD lives, if punishment befalls you: an oath meaning "it will not befall you"
decisions.reason: In a Hebrew oath, "if" with the rest of a curse left unsaid means "certainly not": "may God deal with me if it happens". So Saul swears that she will not be punished (14:45; 19:6).

decisions.choice: Saul swears by the LORD: he calls on the LORD to protect what the LORD's law forbids
decisions.reason: The LORD had not answered Saul (verse 6), yet he uses the LORD's name to promise safety for consulting the dead, which the law punishes (Leviticus 20:6, 27). The king who enforced the law now promises to set it aside.

decisions.choice: punishment: guilt and the penalty it brings
decisions.reason: The word can mean the wrong itself, the guilt for it, or its punishment (Genesis 4:13). With "befall you" it means the penalty.

decisions.choice: made a promise to her in the name of the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable explains "swore by the LORD" as a promise made in his name.

records.source: וַתֹּ֨אמֶר֙ הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה אֶת־מִ֖י אַֽעֲלֶה־לָּ֑ךְ וַיֹּ֕אמֶר אֶת־שְׁמוּאֵ֖ל הַֽעֲלִי־לִֽי׃
records.gloss: And said the woman, Whom shall I bring up for you? And he said, Samuel bring up for me.
pieces: Then the woman asked, "Whom should I bring up for you?" He said, "Bring up Samuel for me."

L.11: Then the woman said, "Whom shall I bring up for you?" And he said, "Bring up Samuel for me."

R.11: Then the woman asked, "Who do you want me to bring up?" Saul answered, "Bring up Samuel."

decisions.choice: Samuel bring up for me: Samuel's name comes first, for emphasis
decisions.reason: Saul puts the name before the verb: it is Samuel he wants and no one else.

decisions.choice: Samuel: the prophet who had made Saul king and then rejected him
decisions.reason: Samuel had anointed Saul and told him what to do (10:1-8), and then told him that the LORD had rejected him (13:13-14; 15:26-28). After that Samuel did not see Saul again until the day he died (15:35). Saul turns to him because God will not answer him.

decisions.choice: Saul answered
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker.

records.source: וַתֵּ֤רֶא הָֽאִשָּׁה֙ אֶת־שְׁמוּאֵ֔ל וַתִּזְעַ֖ק בְּק֣וֹל גָּד֑וֹל וַתֹּאמֶר֩ הָאִשָּׁ֨ה אֶל־שָׁא֧וּל לֵאמֹ֛ר לָ֥מָּה רִמִּיתָ֖נִי וְאַתָּ֥ה שָׁאֽוּל׃
records.gloss: And saw the woman Samuel and cried out with a voice great; and said the woman to Saul, saying, Why have you deceived me? And you [are] Saul.
pieces: When the woman saw Samuel, she screamed, and she said to Saul, "Why have you deceived me? You are Saul!"

L.12: And the woman saw Samuel, and she cried out with a loud voice. And the woman said to Saul, "Why have you deceived me? You are Saul!"

R.12: When the woman saw Samuel, she screamed loudly. She said to Saul, "Why did you trick me? You are Saul!"

decisions.choice: the woman saw Samuel: the narrator presents the figure as Samuel himself
alternatives: a spirit that only appeared to be Samuel
decisions.reason: From here on the narrator calls the one who appears "Samuel" (verses 12, 14, 15, 16, 20), not a spirit or an appearance of him. He speaks as Samuel spoke, repeats Samuel's own words of 15:28, and says what will happen, and it does happen (31:1-6). The woman's terrified cry may show that this was not what she expected from her practice. The text does not explain how it happened, and it never says that her arts had power to bring up the dead; the plainest reading is that God allowed Samuel to come and speak one last word of judgment. Others have read it as a spirit pretending to be Samuel, or as a trick by the woman; the narrator gives no hint of either. Nothing here approves of consulting the dead, which this book and the law condemn (verse 3; 1 Chronicles 10:13).

decisions.choice: you are Saul: she now knows who he is
decisions.reason: The text does not say how she knew. It may be that only the king would ask for Samuel, or that the appearance itself made it plain.

decisions.choice: deceived me: tricked me
decisions.reason: Saul had hidden who he was (verse 8). Now she fears that the king who banned her trade has caught her at it.

decisions.choice: screamed
decisions.reason: "Cried out with a loud voice" is a scream of terror, and Balanced and Readable say so.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר לָ֥הּ הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ אַל־תִּֽירְאִ֖י כִּ֣י מָ֣ה רָאִ֑ית וַתֹּ֤אמֶר הָֽאִשָּׁה֙ אֶל־שָׁא֔וּל אֱלֹהִ֥ים רָאִ֖יתִי עֹלִ֥ים מִן־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And said to her the king, Do not fear; for what have you seen? And said the woman to Saul, God I have seen coming up from the earth.
pieces: The king told her, "Do not be afraid. What are you seeing?" The woman answered Saul, "I see a divine being coming up out of the ground."

L.13: And the king said to her, "Do not be afraid. But what have you seen?" And the woman said to Saul, "I see a god coming up out of the earth."

R.13: The king said to her, "Do not be afraid. What do you see?" The woman answered Saul, "I see a being like a god coming up out of the ground."

decisions.choice: a god: a being from beyond the human world, here the spirit of a dead person
decisions.reason: The word is the one usually used for God or for gods. It can also name other beings above ordinary humans: the heavenly beings around God (Psalm 82:1, 6), or someone who stands in God's place (Exodus 4:16; 7:1). Isaiah 8:19 seems to use it for the spirits of the dead whom people consulted. Here the woman sees something more than human and uses this word for it. The word is plural in form, as it always is, and the verb "coming up" is plural too, so it may mean "gods", more than one figure; but Saul at once asks "What is his form?", and she describes one man (verse 14). So she most likely means one being. What she meant by the word is not certain.

decisions.choice: coming up out of the earth: rising from the place of the dead
decisions.reason: The dead were thought to be beneath the earth, in Sheol (2:6). The figure comes up from there.

decisions.choice: do not be afraid; but what have you seen?
decisions.reason: Saul does not deny who he is. He calms her and presses on to what he came for. The woman seems to see, while Saul does not; he must ask her.

decisions.choice: a god (Literal); a divine being (Balanced); a being like a god (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the bare word. Balanced and Readable say "divine being" and "being like a god" so that readers do not think she saw the LORD or a false god, since she means a figure greater than human. "I see" is used at every level because the verb describes what is in front of her now.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָהּ֙ מַֽה־תָּאֳר֔וֹ וַתֹּ֗אמֶר אִ֤ישׁ זָקֵן֙ עֹלֶ֔ה וְה֥וּא עֹטֶ֖ה מְעִ֑יל וַיֵּ֤דַע שָׁאוּל֙ כִּֽי־שְׁמוּאֵ֣ל ה֔וּא וַיִּקֹּ֥ד אַפַּ֛יִם אַ֖רְצָה וַיִּשְׁתָּֽחוּ׃ס
records.gloss: And he said to her, What [is] his form? And she said, A man old [is] coming up, and he [is] wrapped [in] a robe. And knew Saul that Samuel [was] it, and he bowed [with] face to the ground and prostrated himself.
pieces: He asked her, "What does he look like?" She said, "An old man is coming up, and he is wrapped in a robe." Then Saul knew that it was Samuel. He bowed low, face to the ground, and lay down before him.

L.14: And he said to her, "What [is] his form?" And she said, "An old man is coming up, and he is wrapped in a robe." And Saul knew that it [was] Samuel, and he bowed with [his] face to the ground and prostrated himself.

R.14: Saul asked her, "What does he look like?" She answered, "An old man is coming up. He is wearing a robe." Then Saul knew it was Samuel. He bowed down low with his face to the ground.

decisions.choice: a robe: the prophet's robe Samuel was known by
decisions.reason: As a boy Samuel wore a little robe his mother made for him each year (2:19). When Saul grabbed the edge of Samuel's robe and it tore, Samuel told him that the LORD had torn the kingdom from him (15:27-28). The same robe now marks him out, and he repeats that word (verse 17).

decisions.choice: Saul knew that it was Samuel: from her description
decisions.reason: Saul asks what the figure looks like, which suggests that he does not see it himself. He recognizes Samuel from what the woman tells him.

decisions.choice: he bowed with his face to the ground and prostrated himself: deep respect
decisions.reason: Bowing to the ground was the honor shown to a king, a prophet or a superior (20:41; 24:9; 25:23). The king who would not listen to Samuel bows to him now.

decisions.choice: lay down before him (Balanced); bowed down low (Readable)
decisions.reason: Two verbs describe one act of bowing; Readable uses one. Balanced and Readable say "what does he look like" for "what is his form".

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר שְׁמוּאֵל֙ אֶל־שָׁא֔וּל לָ֥מָּה הִרְגַּזְתַּ֖נִי לְהַעֲל֣וֹת אֹתִ֑י וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שָׁ֠אוּל צַר־לִ֨י מְאֹ֜ד וּפְלִשְׁתִּ֣ים׀נִלְחָמִ֣ים בִּ֗י וֵֽאלֹהִ֞ים סָ֤ר מֵֽעָלַי֙ וְלֹֽא־עָנָ֣נִי ע֗וֹד גַּ֤ם בְּיַֽד־הַנְּבִיאִם֙ גַּם־בַּ֣חֲלֹמ֔וֹת וָאֶקְרָאֶ֣ה לְךָ֔ לְהוֹדִיעֵ֖נִי מָ֥ה אֶעֱשֶֽׂה׃ס
records.gloss: And said Samuel to Saul, Why have you disturbed me by bringing up me? And said Saul, It is distressing to me greatly, and [the] Philistines [are] fighting against me, and God has turned away from me and not answered me anymore, either by [the] hand of the prophets or by dreams; and I have called you to make known to me what I shall do.
pieces: Samuel asked Saul, "Why have you disturbed me and brought me up?" Saul answered, "I am in deep trouble. The Philistines are making war on me, and God has turned away from me and answers me no longer, whether through the prophets or in dreams. That is why I have called on you, so that you can tell me what I ought to do."

L.15: And Samuel said to Saul, "Why have you disturbed me by bringing me up?" And Saul said, "I am in great distress, for the Philistines are fighting against me, and God has turned away from me and does not answer me anymore, either by the hand of the prophets or by dreams. So I have called you to make known to me what I should do."

R.15: Samuel said to Saul, "Why have you bothered me? Why have you brought me up?" Saul answered, "I am in terrible trouble. The Philistines are fighting against me, and God has left me. He does not answer me anymore, not through prophets and not in dreams. So I called you to tell me what to do."

decisions.choice: disturbed me: stirred me up from my rest
decisions.reason: The verb means to shake or to stir up, here to break the rest of the dead. Isaiah 14:9 uses it of the place of the dead stirred up to meet a fallen king.

decisions.choice: God has turned away from me: what Saul feels is true
decisions.reason: The same verb was used when the Spirit of the LORD turned away from Saul (16:14) and when the LORD was with David but had turned away from Saul (18:12). Samuel answers with the same words in verse 16.

decisions.choice: prophets or dreams: Saul does not mention the Urim
decisions.reason: In verse 6 the narrator lists three ways, dreams, Urim and prophets. Saul names only two. The text does not say why.

decisions.choice: God: the general word for God
decisions.reason: Saul speaks of "God", while Samuel in his answer speaks of the LORD by name (verses 16-19). The two are the same God; the difference may be only one of speech.

decisions.choice: Why have you bothered me? Why have you brought me up?
decisions.reason: Readable splits Samuel's question into two short ones.

records.heading: Samuel's word to Saul

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שְׁמוּאֵ֔ל וְלָ֖מָּה תִּשְׁאָלֵ֑נִי וַיהוָ֛ה סָ֥ר מֵעָלֶ֖יךָ וַיְהִ֥י עָרֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: And said Samuel, And why do you ask me, and Yahweh has turned away from you and become your enemy?
pieces: Samuel said, "Why do you ask me, then, when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has turned away from you and become your enemy?

L.16: And Samuel said, "Then why do you ask me, when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has turned away from you and has become your enemy?

R.16: Samuel said, "Why ask me? {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has left you. He has become your enemy.

decisions.choice: why do you ask me: Samuel has nothing to give apart from the LORD
decisions.reason: Samuel was only ever the LORD's spokesman. If the LORD has turned away from Saul, a dead prophet cannot give him another answer. The word "ask" again sounds like Saul's name (verse 6).

decisions.choice: your enemy
alternatives: has gone over to your neighbor
decisions.reason: The word for "enemy" here is rare; it is found again in Psalm 139:20 and in the Aramaic of Daniel 4:16. The ancient Greek translation reads instead "and has become with your neighbor", which would point ahead to verse 17. The Hebrew text, which governs, has "your enemy". Reviewers should check this note against the textual evidence.

decisions.choice: has turned away from you: Samuel takes up Saul's own words
decisions.reason: Saul had said "God has turned away from me" (verse 15). Samuel agrees, and says more: the LORD is now against him.

decisions.choice: Why ask me? The LORD has left you. He has become your enemy.
decisions.reason: Readable turns the one long question into a short question and two statements. Samuel's speech runs on to verse 19, so the quotation is not closed here.

records.source: וַיַּ֤עַשׂ יְהוָה֙ ל֔וֹ כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּ֣ר בְּיָדִ֑י וַיִּקְרַ֨ע יְהוָ֤ה אֶת־הַמַּמְלָכָה֙ מִיָּדֶ֔ךָ וַֽיִּתְּנָ֖הּ לְרֵעֲךָ֥ לְדָוִֽד׃
records.gloss: And has done Yahweh for him as he spoke by my hand, and has torn Yahweh the kingdom from your hand and has given it to your neighbor, to David.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has done for {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} exactly what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said through me. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has torn the kingdom from your hand and given it to your neighbor, to David.

L.17: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has done for {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke by my hand: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has torn the kingdom out of your hand and given it to your neighbor, to David.

R.17: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has done for {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said through me. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has torn the kingdom away from you and given it to someone else, to David.

decisions.choice: for himself
alternatives: the LORD has done to you
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "Yahweh has done for him", which is best taken as "for himself": the LORD has carried out his own purpose. Some Hebrew manuscripts and the ancient Greek translation read "to you", "the LORD has done to you as he said". The Hebrew text governs. Reviewers should check this note against the textual evidence.

decisions.choice: has torn the kingdom from your hand and given it to your neighbor: Samuel's words of 15:28
decisions.reason: When Saul tore Samuel's robe, Samuel said, "The LORD has torn the kingdom of Israel from you today and has given it to your neighbor, who is better than you" (15:28). Then the neighbor was not named; now he is: David.

decisions.choice: by my hand: through me
decisions.reason: The "hand" of a prophet is the means by which the LORD speaks (verse 15, "by the hand of the prophets").

decisions.choice: someone else, to David
decisions.reason: "Neighbor" here means another man, not one who lives nearby. Readable says "someone else" and keeps the name.

records.source: כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא־שָׁמַ֨עְתָּ֙ בְּק֣וֹל יְהוָ֔ה וְלֹֽא־עָשִׂ֥יתָ חֲרוֹן־אַפּ֖וֹ בַּעֲמָלֵ֑ק עַל־כֵּן֙ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה עָשָֽׂה־לְךָ֥ יְהוָ֖ה הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: Because not you listened to [the] voice of Yahweh and not you carried out [the] burning of his anger against Amalek, therefore the thing this has done to you Yahweh the day this.
pieces: Because you did not obey {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and did not carry out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} fierce anger against Amalek, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has done this to you today.

L.18: Because you did not listen to the voice of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and did not carry out the burning of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger against Amalek, therefore {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has done this thing to you this day.

R.18: You did not obey {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He was very angry with the Amalekites, but you did not punish them as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} commanded. That is why {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has done this to you today.

decisions.choice: you did not listen ... against Amalek: Saul's failure in chapter 15
decisions.reason: The LORD had commanded Saul to devote Amalek to destruction (15:3), but Saul spared King Agag and the best of the animals (15:9). Samuel told him then that to obey is better than sacrifice, and that because he had rejected the LORD's word, the LORD had rejected him as king (15:22-23, 26).

decisions.choice: listen to the voice of the LORD: obey the LORD
decisions.reason: To "listen to the voice" of someone is to do what they say (15:19-20, 22). The phrase comes back in verses 21-23, where the woman and Saul "listen to the voice" of each other.

decisions.choice: carry out the burning of his anger: carry out his fierce judgment
decisions.reason: "Burning of anger" is the LORD's fierce anger against wrong. Saul was to be the means of the LORD's judgment on Amalek (Exodus 17:14; Deuteronomy 25:17-19), and he did not do it fully.

decisions.choice: You did not obey ... That is why
decisions.reason: Readable puts the reason first in its own sentences, and says what carrying out the LORD's anger meant: punishing the Amalekites as he had commanded.

records.source: וְיִתֵּ֣ן יְ֠הוָה גַּ֣ם אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל עִמְּךָ֙ בְּיַד־פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וּמָחָ֕ר אַתָּ֥ה וּבָנֶ֖יךָ עִמִּ֑י גַּ֚ם אֶת־מַחֲנֵ֣ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל יִתֵּ֥ן יְהוָ֖ה בְּיַד־פְּלִשְׁתִּֽים׃
records.gloss: And will give Yahweh also Israel with you into [the] hand of [the] Philistines; and tomorrow you and your sons [will be] with me; also the camp of Israel will give Yahweh into [the] hand of [the] Philistines.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will also hand Israel over to the Philistines along with you. Tomorrow you and your sons will be with me. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will hand the army of Israel over to the Philistines as well."

L.19: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will also give Israel with you into the hand of the Philistines, and tomorrow you and your sons [will be] with me. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will also give the camp of Israel into the hand of the Philistines."

R.19: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will let the Philistines defeat both you and the people of Israel. Tomorrow you and your sons will be with me among the dead. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will let the Philistines defeat Israel's army."

decisions.choice: tomorrow you and your sons will be with me: you will die
decisions.reason: Samuel is among the dead, so to be "with" him is to die. Saul and three of his sons die in the battle on Gilboa (31:2-6).

decisions.choice: with me: among the dead, not a statement about reward or punishment
decisions.reason: Samuel says only that Saul will join him in death. The words do not say what that state is like, or that Saul and Samuel will share the same lot beyond death.

decisions.choice: tomorrow: the next day
decisions.reason: The word means the coming day. The battle is told in chapter 31; chapters 29 and 30 go back to tell what David was doing in the same days.

decisions.choice: the LORD will give ... the LORD will give: the judgment falls on Israel too
decisions.reason: The sentence begins and ends with the LORD handing Israel over. The people as well as their king will suffer defeat (31:1, 7).

decisions.choice: with me among the dead
decisions.reason: Readable adds "among the dead" so that the meaning of "with me" is clear. It closes Samuel's speech, which began in verse 15.

records.source: וַיְמַהֵ֣ר שָׁא֗וּל וַיִּפֹּ֤ל מְלֹא־קֽוֹמָתוֹ֙ אַ֔רְצָה וַיִּרָ֥א מְאֹ֖ד מִדִּבְרֵ֣י שְׁמוּאֵ֑ל גַּם־כֹּ֨חַ֙ לֹא־הָ֣יָה ב֔וֹ כִּ֣י לֹ֤א אָכַל֙ לֶ֔חֶם כָּל־הַיּ֖וֹם וְכָל־הַלָּֽיְלָה׃
records.gloss: And hurried Saul and fell [the] fullness of his stature to the ground, and was afraid greatly because of [the] words of Samuel; also strength not was in him, for not had he eaten food all the day and all the night.
pieces: At once Saul fell full length on the ground, terrified by Samuel's words. There was no strength left in him, because he had eaten nothing all that day and all that night.

L.20: And Saul quickly fell at his full length to the ground and was very afraid because of the words of Samuel. There was also no strength in him, for he had not eaten food all the day and all the night.

R.20: Right away Saul fell flat on the ground. He was terrified by what Samuel had said. He also had no strength, because he had not eaten anything all day and all night.

decisions.choice: the fullness of his stature: the tall king fell full length
decisions.reason: Saul was taller than anyone else in Israel (9:2; 10:23). The full height that once marked him out now lies stretched on the ground.

decisions.choice: he had not eaten food all the day and all the night: he had been fasting
decisions.reason: The text does not say why Saul had not eaten. It may have been a fast before seeking an answer from God, or fear and strain before the battle (compare 14:24).

decisions.choice: hurried: at once
decisions.reason: The verb "hurry" used before another verb means that the action happened immediately.

decisions.choice: fell flat on the ground
decisions.reason: Readable says "flat" for "the fullness of his stature".

records.source: וַתָּב֤וֹא הָֽאִשָּׁה֙ אֶל־שָׁא֔וּל וַתֵּ֖רֶא כִּי־נִבְהַ֣ל מְאֹ֑ד וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֗יו הִנֵּ֨ה שָׁמְעָ֤ה שִׁפְחָֽתְךָ֙ בְּקוֹלֶ֔ךָ וָאָשִׂ֤ים נַפְשִׁי֙ בְּכַפִּ֔י וָֽאֶשְׁמַע֙ אֶת־דְּבָרֶ֔יךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבַּ֖רְתָּ אֵלָֽי׃
records.gloss: And came the woman to Saul and saw that he was terrified greatly, and she said to him, Behold, has listened your maidservant to your voice, and I have put my life in my palm, and I have listened to your words which you spoke to me.
pieces: The woman came to Saul and saw that he was badly shaken, and she said to him, "Look, your servant has done what you asked. I took my life in my hands and did what you told me.

L.21: And the woman came to Saul and saw that he was greatly terrified, and she said to him, "Look, your maidservant has listened to your voice. I have put my life in my palm and have listened to your words that you spoke to me.

R.21: The woman came over to Saul. When she saw how terrified he was, she said, "Listen, I did what you asked me to do. I risked my life to do what you told me.

decisions.choice: I have put my life in my palm: I risked my life
decisions.reason: To hold one's life in one's hand is to put it in danger (Judges 12:3; 19:5 in this book). She broke the king's own ban, which could cost her life (verse 9).

decisions.choice: your maidservant: a humble way of saying "I"
decisions.reason: The woman uses the word for a servant girl, as Hannah did (1:18) and Abigail did before David (25:24-28).

decisions.choice: has listened to your voice: the theme of listening
decisions.reason: Samuel has just said that Saul did not listen to the LORD's voice (verse 18). The woman says that she listened to Saul's voice, and she asks him in turn to listen to hers (verse 22). In verse 23 Saul at last listens to them.

decisions.choice: the woman came to Saul: she had stepped away or was apart from him
decisions.reason: The text suggests she was at some distance while Samuel spoke, but it does not say where.

decisions.choice: has done what you asked; did what you told me
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "listened to your voice" meant here: she did what he asked. Readable says "I" for "your maidservant". Her speech runs on into verse 22, so the quotation is not closed here.

records.source: וְעַתָּ֗ה שְׁמַֽע־נָ֤א גַם־אַתָּה֙ בְּק֣וֹל שִׁפְחָתֶ֔ךָ וְאָשִׂ֧מָה לְפָנֶ֛יךָ פַּת־לֶ֖חֶם וֶאֱכ֑וֹל וִיהִ֤י בְךָ֙ כֹּ֔חַ כִּ֥י תֵלֵ֖ךְ בַּדָּֽרֶךְ׃
records.gloss: And now listen please also you to [the] voice of your maidservant, and let me set before you a morsel of bread, and eat, and let there be in you strength, for you will go on the way.
pieces: So now, please, listen to your servant in turn. Let me set a little food in front of you. Eat it, so that you will have strength when you go on your way."

L.22: And now, please, you also listen to the voice of your maidservant, and let me set before you a morsel of bread, and eat, so that there may be strength in you when you go on [your] way."

R.22: Now please do what I ask. Let me give you something to eat. Eat it so that you will be strong enough to travel back."

decisions.choice: a morsel of bread: a little food, a modest way of offering a meal
decisions.reason: Abraham offers "a morsel of bread" and then serves a whole calf (Genesis 18:5-8). The woman does the same in verse 24. "Bread" stands for food in general.

decisions.choice: you also: listen to me as I listened to you
decisions.reason: She asks for the same obedience she has shown him (verse 21).

decisions.choice: a little food; something to eat
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "food" for "bread" here, since a meal of meat and bread follows. Readable says "travel back" for "go on your way", the way back to Saul's camp.

records.source: וַיְמָאֵ֗ן וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ לֹ֣א אֹכַ֔ל וַיִּפְרְצוּ־ב֤וֹ עֲבָדָיו֙ וְגַם־הָ֣אִשָּׁ֔ה וַיִּשְׁמַ֖ע לְקֹלָ֑ם וַיָּ֨קָם֙ מֵֽהָאָ֔רֶץ וַיֵּ֖שֶׁב אֶל־הַמִּטָּֽה׃
records.gloss: And he refused and said, Not I will eat. And urged him his servants and also the woman, and he listened to their voice; and he arose from the ground and sat on the bed.
pieces: He refused and said, "I will not eat." But his servants joined the woman in pressing him, and he listened to them. He got up from the ground and sat on the couch.

L.23: But he refused and said, "I will not eat." But his servants, and the woman also, urged him, and he listened to their voice. And he rose from the ground and sat on the bed.

R.23: Saul refused. He said, "I will not eat." But his servants and the woman kept on urging him, and at last he did what they said. He got up from the ground and sat on the bed.

decisions.choice: urged him: pressed him hard
decisions.reason: The verb means "break through", and with a person it means to press someone until they give way (2 Samuel 13:25, 27).

decisions.choice: the bed: a couch or bed along the wall, used for sitting or lying
decisions.reason: The word names a bed or a couch for reclining (Esther 1:6; Amos 6:4). Saul moves from lying on the ground to sitting up to eat.

decisions.choice: he listened to their voice
decisions.reason: As in verses 18, 21 and 22: Saul, who did not listen to the LORD's voice, listens to his servants and the woman.

decisions.choice: couch
decisions.reason: Balanced says "couch" because Saul sits on it to eat. Literal and Readable keep "bed".

records.source: וְלָאִשָּׁ֤ה עֵֽגֶל־מַרְבֵּק֙ בַּבַּ֔יִת וַתְּמַהֵ֖ר וַתִּזְבָּחֵ֑הוּ וַתִּקַּח־קֶ֣מַח וַתָּ֔לָשׁ וַתֹּפֵ֖הוּ מַצּֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: And the woman had a calf of [the] stall in the house, and she hurried and slaughtered it, and took flour and kneaded and baked it [into] unleavened bread.
pieces: The woman had a fattened calf in the house, and she quickly slaughtered it. She took flour, kneaded it, and baked bread without yeast.

L.24: Now the woman had a stall-fed calf in the house, and she quickly slaughtered it. And she took flour and kneaded [it] and baked it [into] unleavened bread.

R.24: The woman had a calf in her house that she had been fattening. She quickly killed it. Then she took some flour, made it into dough, and baked flat bread without yeast.

decisions.choice: a stall-fed calf: an animal kept and fattened for a special meal
decisions.reason: A calf fattened in a stall was costly food, served to honored guests (Genesis 18:7; Amos 6:4). The woman gives Saul her best.

decisions.choice: slaughtered: killed for eating
decisions.reason: The verb is often used for killing an animal in sacrifice, but it also means slaughter for an ordinary meal (Deuteronomy 12:15, 21).

decisions.choice: unleavened bread: bread made quickly, without waiting for it to rise
decisions.reason: Bread without yeast could be baked at once, as when Lot fed his guests (Genesis 19:3) or Israel left Egypt in haste (Exodus 12:39).

decisions.choice: made it into dough; flat bread without yeast
decisions.reason: Readable explains kneading and unleavened bread in everyday words.

records.source: וַתַּגֵּ֧שׁ לִפְנֵֽי־שָׁא֛וּל וְלִפְנֵ֥י עֲבָדָ֖יו וַיֹּאכֵ֑לוּ וַיָּקֻ֥מוּ וַיֵּלְכ֖וּ בַּלַּ֥יְלָה הַהֽוּא׃פ
records.gloss: And she brought [it] before Saul and before his servants, and they ate; and they arose and went in the night that.
pieces: She set it before Saul and his servants, and they ate. Then they got up and left that same night.

L.25: And she brought [it] before Saul and before his servants, and they ate. Then they rose and went away that night.

R.25: She served the food to Saul and his servants, and they ate it. Then they got up and left while it was still night.

decisions.choice: that night: the story begins and ends in darkness
decisions.reason: Saul came to the woman by night (verse 8) and leaves by night. The next time he appears, he is fighting his last battle (31:1-6).

decisions.choice: she brought it before Saul ... and they ate: the woman serves her guests
decisions.reason: The woman who was afraid of the king ends by caring for him like a host. This meal is the last thing told of Saul before his death.

decisions.choice: while it was still night
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that they set off before daylight.
